active.packageId: ASP.NET Core API and Angular 22 presentation migration
active.scope: Canonical Angular route ownership is in place. AuditSphereOps.Web and its Razor source remain restored as rollback/reference. API.Tests and E2E.Tests use API-only hosts. All 82 removed E2E methods have assertion crosswalks. The 76-row source/action inventory has one parity-verified row and 75 partial reviews, with no unanalyzed rows. All 28 supporting files have partial reviews and remain open for parity or retirement acceptance. Focused partial-review evidence covers Statement Drilldown, Trial Balance Intake, risk routing, shared confirmation callers (cancel across both callers and revocation dual-review guards), acceptance checklist workspace/role, Global Search identity/invoice/input/cap/audience, technical-library boundaries and representative role/scope combinations, portfolio aggregates, contact-create recovery, authenticated and unauthenticated canonical/preview root routing, and the Operations firm-wide Administrator denial message. At c5887ee8, Global Search now orders tied lead names by immutable record ID before its six-hit cap; a PostgreSQL case seeds eight equal-name leads in reverse ID order, verifies the six stable lowest IDs on repeated searches and confirms truncation. The query class passed 17/17 and the API-host browser class passed 4/4. Built-in browser read-only search returned one authorized Firm finance page result; the temporary search state was cleared. Global Search technical-library and supported-page destinations have Angular Staff browser journeys; PostgreSQL tests cover library audience/firm isolation and cap/truncation for all seven result kinds; the Angular UI displays refinement hints for capped library and page results; a PostgreSQL-backed browser journey verifies Client, Engagement, PBC category order against the legacy kind grouping. At 0fa19701, 31 authorized matches per Client, Engagement, PBC and Invoice prove six-hit caps, truncation, and stable tie ordering beyond the 25-row candidate window. At abb798ea, the PostgreSQL portfolio export test proves exactly 1,000 client rows succeed and 1,001 are refused while narrowed export and formula neutralization remain covered. At 4fc08ea5, the API-host refusal and Angular recovery boundaries are pinned: the 1,001-client API response is typed HTTP 400 JSON without a CSV attachment, and the UI clears the refusal after a narrowed search reload and explicit export retry. The built-in browser Operations view remains correctly denied to the scoped Staff preview identity and shows no operation data or commands; authorization was not changed. At a1076925, the Operations page also removes its refresh action after the safe 403/404 Administrator-denial state; temporary 503 failures retain an explicit retry. Angular operations tests passed 6/6, the PostgreSQL-backed API-host Operations journey passed 1/1, and the built-in browser confirmed the Staff denial message without the refresh control or operation data. The production Angular build passed with the pre-existing commercial-settings stylesheet budget warning. At f7bc5e4e, Operations browser coverage verifies both concurrent expired-grant revocation and cross-firm guessed-ID isolation. Expiry advances the session epoch once and records one event; the stale browser receives a safe 401/409. A current-firm Administrator cannot list, retry or cancel a foreign-firm operation by ID; no operation details leak and the foreign record remains unchanged. Browser recovery covers synthetic 503/retry, malformed 200 and 401 session clearing. At fa386c32, the full browser class passed 4/4 in 1m25s. It verifies the 15-second timeout and explicit retry, plus persisted session-epoch revocation during an in-flight search: the protected API returns 401, search content clears, and the delayed hit cannot restore stale content. The revocation case passed 1/1 in 29s. Existing Angular unit tests cover cancellation on invalidation and were not rerun; cross-route revocation matrices remain open. Other slices retain their documented evidence limits. A local Test-profile Web rollback-host smoke at code commit a1076925 built Release with zero warnings/errors and rendered the Blazor / home and /app Portfolio routes; the unsigned portfolio showed Sign-in required with no actor or client data, and the Blazor SignalR connection reached HTTP 101. The application log recorded HTTP 404 for an unmapped /app path; the built-in browser blocked rendering that navigation, so only the server response is counted. The build included another agent’s uncommitted consolidation query edit, which these routes did not exercise and which was excluded from our commits. This is local route evidence only, not production rollback/canary acceptance. Overall migration acceptance and Blazor retirement are NOT_READY. At 788bc218, firm-books rejection requires a bounded reviewer-authored reason, same-preparer review remains denied, and same-day expense journal identity collisions are fixed; the focused Angular, PostgreSQL domain and API-host browser checks pass. Finance source review and whole-application migration acceptance remain partial. At 3bff1eb1, the firm-books Angular/PostgreSQL boundary cohort passed 2/2: malformed and oversized uploads, foreign-versus-guessed-ID denial equivalence, unchanged foreign state, session-epoch content clearing, and repeated post response/persisted-single-post verification. Firm-books source parity remains partial; the next focused finance work is broader ledger and invoice authorization/recovery, then remaining whole-application AS-PAR-002 rows. At 7834ddec, the PostgreSQL Angular invoice lifecycle/scope/recovery cohort passed 3/3, focused capability tests passed 4/4, the production Angular build passed with the existing stylesheet warning, and EF reported no pending model changes. At 1b439f25, a browser journey compared a real foreign-firm invoice with a random ID for detail, approve, post and send; every pair returned identical HTTP 403 and the foreign invoice remained unchanged. At 7b709324, malformed/empty cursors returned identical safe 400 responses and a simulated receipt-history 503 recovered on retry. At de27c966, receipt and credit-history simulated 503s both preserved existing rows and recovered on retry. At 793d29dd, a held receipt-history response was released after navigating to another client invoice and did not restore the previous client rows; the focused journey passed 1/1 in 35s. Broader FinanceManager/FinanceReviewer and client/firm scope combinations, remaining uncertain billing outcomes remain open; finance source rows remain partial. At code/test commit cfbeed2d, the firm-ledger boundary journey also verifies a whitespace-only close reason cannot be submitted in Angular, direct API returns safe 400 ledger.invalid, and PostgreSQL remains OPEN at revision 1 with no close decision. State-conflict/provider failure recovery, broader finance role/scope, and the other stated AS-PAR-002 rows remain open. At code/test commit e3301035, the invoice-history browser journey also holds an authorized real API 200, revokes the session epoch, verifies invoice/session requests return 401 and Access unavailable is shown, then releases the delayed response and confirms no invoice or receipt markers return. The isolated journey passed 1/1; Angular production build passed with the existing commercial-settings stylesheet budget warning. Remaining finance role/scope combinations and uncertain outcomes, other AS-PAR-002 rows, production and owner acceptance remain open. At code/test commit 84ce3567, AngularInvoiceScopeJourneyTests also verifies client-scoped FinanceReviewer approval for its assigned client, sibling-client invoice route denial without content leakage, 403 for direct sibling invoice approval, and unchanged DRAFT state; the isolated PostgreSQL/API-host Playwright journey passed 1/1. Complete firm-wide/client-scope combinations and remaining billing outcomes stay open. At code/test commit bc276764, AngularBillingWorkspaceJourneyTests also simulates an accepted receipt allocation with a lost browser response, requires persisted-state reconciliation, verifies the receipt row reflects 25.00 allocated before clearing the unresolved draft, and confirms one API call and one database allocation. The isolated PostgreSQL/API-host journey passed 1/1 in 33s. Other uncertain billing outcomes, full finance role/scope and broader AS-PAR-002 remain open. At code/test commit 9207a475, FirmLedgerCloseBlockedByUnpostedJournalCanRecoverAfterPosting passed 1/1 in 29s: an unposted journal blocks close without mutation; after the manager submits/posts and the reviewer approves, retry closes once at revision 2 with reason and actor persisted. Provider failure and concurrent state-conflict recovery remain open. At code/test commit aca91b12, AngularFirmBooksJourneyTests passed 1/1 in 35s. It verifies a post request not sent to the API reconciles to APPROVED before an acknowledged retry, then verifies an accepted post with a lost response refreshes the exact expense as POSTED without resending; PostgreSQL contains one posting and repeated direct post commands are idempotent. Other unknown outcomes for record, submit and review remain open. At code/test commit fa9c21d2, AngularFirmWideScopeJourneyTests passed 1/1 in 42s. Firm-wide FinanceManager and FinanceReviewer get separate prepare/review capability flags; client-scoped Manager and Partner are denied with 403, and an external Client identity is kept in the Client portal and denied direct firm-books API access. Denials leak no expense marker and the persisted draft remains unchanged. At 8faa79b2, a PostgreSQL-backed Angular browser journey proves a client-scoped FinanceManager can record and allocate a receipt and issue a credit note for the assigned client, while four sibling/cross-client API mutations return 403 without sibling data changes. Invoice role/scope and uncertain-outcome coverage remains partial; the complete suite remains the earlier 1001/1001 checkpoint at ead85032. At d7854fc8, a PostgreSQL-backed Angular browser journey verifies lost approve/post/send responses after accepted server transitions. Each lifecycle action remains blocked until explicit persisted-state refresh, and only one request is sent. AS-PAR-002 and Blazor retirement remain partial/NOT_READY. At 356d48a9, a PostgreSQL-backed Angular role matrix verifies firm-wide FinanceManager read-only access, FinanceReviewer close authority, and Partner denial with no finance data or period mutation. The wider migration remains partial and the Blazor retirement gate remains NOT_READY. At pushed code commit d21d0382, the expense submit/review lost-response journey passed 1/1: a pre-dispatch submit remained DRAFT until persisted-state verification and explicit retry acknowledgment; an accepted review with a dropped response was verified as APPROVED without resend, with one journal and no browser errors. Expense-record creation recovery remains open.

remainingLocalWork.item: AS-PAR-002 — remaining whole-application scope and revocation coverage
remainingLocalWork.details: Verified slices cover firm/client/engagement/group grant scoping; protected details, queues, exports and route reads; revocation denials; stale-content clearing; PBC request/inbox role, recipient, draft, sibling-engagement, cross-client and revocation boundaries; archive/review responsive stale-route cases; an accounting task-owner projection limited to current engagement grants; Angular release-candidate scope, expired-attestation blocking, stale-route clearing and post-revocation hiding; same-client sibling-engagement isolation for workpaper, finding, population and accounting mapping; completion, audit-plan and adopted-fieldwork route clearing/recovery; reviewer-only fieldwork data redaction and command denial; materiality self-approval suppression; refresh-time clearing after revocation for workpaper/finding/audit-plan; exact-source human audit conclusions; reviewed fieldwork/workpaper freezing across reload; package, journal, FX-remeasurement, package-review selection recovery and client-management artifact/decision parity; accounting evidence, period, record-queue, workspace, restatement and roll-forward behavior; prior-continuance evidence-reference retention, reviewed blocked-engagement draft creation, Partner activation review, receipt recovery and revocation clearing, and exact-target confirmation review for local access revocation and lead qualification. All 39 removed ClientScopeJourneyTests, all 13 AuditAndReleaseJourneyTests and all 19 FinancialArtifactJourneyTests methods have assertion crosswalks; the removed-suite E2E method crosswalk is 82/82. AS-PAR-002 remains partial: all 76 source/action rows have dispositions (one parity-verified and 75 partial), and the 28 supporting-file reviews remain partial. Complete assertion-level authorization and recovery crosswalks are still required. The Release candidate now has a PostgreSQL-backed Angular issue and lost-response assertion that confirms persisted ISSUED state, sends one request, and creates one release event and durable operation. Broad retry/idempotency and corresponding HTTP/browser positive-negative checks across remaining actions are still open. A dedicated API-host Angular firm-books journey verifies evidence capture, required reviewer-authored rejection, same-preparer API denial, a second same-day expense submission, independent approval/posting and balanced trial balance; the three finance source/action rows remain partial. The old timestamp-prefix journal-number collision was fixed by including the full expense GUID. Finance malformed/oversized input, cross-firm isolation, retry/revocation and invoice lifecycle gaps remain open. Full AS-PAR-002 acceptance remains open. A focused direct Global Search API browser journey now verifies assigned-client hits, sibling-client and foreign-firm no-hit/no-count behavior, ClientUser denial, revoked-grant empty results, and stale-session 401; ranking/candidate behavior and exhaustive role/scope cases remain open; technical-library audience and firm isolation now have focused coverage. A PostgreSQL-backed GlobalSearchQueryTests invoice case now verifies FinanceManager client scope, ordinary Staff denial, firm-wide FinanceReviewer in-firm visibility, and foreign-firm invoice exclusion; the 11-test query class passed. Remaining result-kind ranking/cap behavior, exhaustive role/scope, empty/error recovery, and assistive-technology coverage remain open. A PostgreSQL-backed portfolio browser journey now checks direct workspace API aggregate counts with sibling-client data present on canonical and /ui routes; it passed 2/2 and reports only the assigned client, engagement, candidate and release totals. At abb798ea, PortfolioWorkspaceTests and PortfolioQueryTests passed 5/5 and now prove exactly 1,000 client rows are exportable while 1,001 fail closed with export.limit. Global Search now has direct API assertions for short and overlong terms and a PostgreSQL test for the six-lead result cap with truncation; GlobalSearchJourneyTests passed 2/2 and GlobalSearchQueryTests passed 12/12. Ranking/candidate behavior across result kinds, exhaustive roles/scopes and additional error/recovery cases remain open; technical-library audience, publication and firm isolation now have focused PostgreSQL query coverage. The existing AngularClientContactCreationJourneyTests cohort was rerun and passed 2/2 on canonical and /ui routes, covering draft restore, reviewed primary replacement, lost-response receipt reconciliation without duplication, and grant-revocation clearing; UI validation/conflict rendering remains open; PostgreSQL service tests cover invalid field samples and stale-generation refusal, while exhaustive role/scope and cross-firm HTTP matrices remain open. The parameterless route sweep passed 1/1 for direct / navigation in canonical mode, and a two-mode authenticated root journey passed 2/2 for /app and /ui/app. An additional unauthenticated root journey passed 2/2, verifying a sign-in prompt, exact return destination and successful arrival in each mode; fallback-host behavior remains open. The Operations page denial copy is pinned by a passing browser assertion; the existing protected action journey confirms firm-wide Administrator access. At code commit cb4efe8f, an expired Administrator grant is revoked once under concurrent browser/API requests, advances the session epoch once and records one EXPIRY event; the stale Operations read returns a safe 401/409 with no operation data. Cross-firm Operations list/retry/cancel isolation now has browser coverage; cross-firm boundaries for other capabilities, concurrent or ambiguous recovery and quarantine paths remain open. The Angular browser journey now also verifies a scoped Staff search renders a published ALL_STAFF technical-library hit as a navigable link, opens the exact library route and clears results; GlobalSearchJourneyTests passed 2/2. Ranking/candidate limits across result kinds, exhaustive role/scope and complete accessibility/recovery acceptance remain open. The 48s GlobalSearchJourneyTests rerun also verifies the supported Practice time page result opens /app/practice/time and clears search after navigation. Per-kind ranking/candidate limits, exhaustive roles/scopes and remaining error/recovery cases are still open. The 14-test PostgreSQL search cohort now verifies six-hit truncation for library and page results (seven matching library entries and more than six matching pages); the Angular browser cohort remains 2/2 for library and supported-page navigation. Client, engagement, PBC and invoice cap/ranking behavior and exhaustive role/scope remain open. An Angular browser rerun with seven published library matches now confirms six visible links and the refinement hint while preserving navigation to the selected exact entry; GlobalSearchJourneyTests passed 2/2 in 47s. Page-only truncation guidance is now verified in Angular: six Page hits return with truncated=true, six links render and the refinement hint appears. PostgreSQL cap/truncation coverage now includes all seven result kinds; client, engagement, PBC and invoice queries each return six of seven authorized matches with truncated=true. At 0fa19701, a PostgreSQL fixture with 31 valid authorized matches per Client, Engagement, PBC request and Invoice verified six-hit caps, truncated=true and stable tie ordering beyond the 25-row candidate window. At c5887ee8, lead results also have a deterministic ID tie-break before the six-hit cap (eight equal-name leads inserted in reverse ID order); GlobalSearchQueryTests passed 17/17 and GlobalSearchJourneyTests passed 4/4. Exhaustive role/scope, broader ranking and additional query/error cases remain open. Search recovery covers synthetic 503/retry, malformed 200 and 401 clearing. At fa386c32, GlobalSearchJourneyTests passed 4/4 in 1m25s, including timeout and explicit-retry recovery plus persisted session-epoch revocation during a pending search. After the protected API returns 401, search content clears and the delayed hit cannot restore stale content; the revocation case passed 1/1 in 29s. Angular unit cancellation tests were not rerun; cross-route revocation matrices remain open. At 8faa79b2, an isolated PostgreSQL/API-host Angular browser journey covers assigned-client invoice receipt recording/allocation and credit-note issuance for a client-scoped FinanceManager, with four sibling/cross-client API mutations denied and no persisted sibling changes. This closes only those scoped billing command checks; complete source/action, role/scope and recovery crosswalks remain open. At d7854fc8, an isolated PostgreSQL/API-host Angular journey covers unknown browser outcomes for accepted invoice approval, posting and sending; each requires explicit state refresh and persists exactly one transition. Other lifecycle, role/scope and recovery crosswalks remain open. At 356d48a9, a PostgreSQL/API-host Angular role journey verifies firm-wide FinanceManager read without close authority, FinanceReviewer close visibility, and safe Partner denial; direct manager close receives 403 and persists no decision. Complete source/action scope and recovery crosswalks remain open.

remainingLocalWork.item: ASP.NET Core API and Angular 22 migration
remainingLocalWork.details: Native API and Angular capability routes, financial review/evidence actions, and scoped portfolio/client/contact/engagement projections have local verification. Canonical Angular route ownership is active. AuditSphereOps.Web and its Razor source remain restored as rollback/reference; API.Tests and E2E.Tests use API-only hosts. The latest complete PostgreSQL-backed Release solution regression is 1001/1001 (API 191/191, Domain 660/660, E2E 150/150) at ead85032de2ccc4d4c8043398fa8471d395376a9 and predates later focused migration slices through b3b4e1e3. At 147ac2a0, Angular tests passed 483/483 across 94 files, the production build passed with a 6.60 kB initial-bundle warning-budget overage, and focused PostgreSQL-backed acceptance, activation, engagement-creation, and completion/file-record reviews have per-slice evidence in this ledger. The completion/file-record cohort passed its focused domain and browser journeys at repository snapshot 2d34fca; its direct amendment/lock browser coverage remains open. The activation follow-on passed 483/483 Angular tests, a focused 2/2 PostgreSQL browser cohort, and the 1/1 PostgreSQL lifecycle gate. The blocked-engagement-creation follow-on passed five PostgreSQL domain tests and a 2/2 browser cohort across both route modes; the production build retains the 6.60 kB budget warning. The complete solution and EF pending-model checks were not rerun. Current-source journeys map all 82/82 removed E2E methods. A dedicated Angular firm-books expense workflow journey passed 1/1 at 5a554a09; finance source reviews remain partial. Client Portal home source/action review passed Angular 491/491, PostgreSQL Domain/API cohorts 3/3 and 2/2, and the API-host client portal journey 1/1; risk routing passed its API-host browser journey 1/1 with persisted band/owner and independent Partner-clearance evidence; a follow-up verifies the assessor sees no self-clear action and a direct self-review command receives 403. Shared confirmation caller review passed Angular CI 491/491, production build, and two PostgreSQL-backed API-host browser journeys for identity/scope display, lead qualification, grant revocation and session invalidation. All these source/action reviews remain partial. Workpaper, ReviewPoint, Records Archive and Release source/action reviews are recorded as PARTIAL; focused PostgreSQL browser evidence passed 5/5 for Workpaper, 1/1 for ReviewPoint, 1/1 for Archive and 2/2 for Release, with a 1/1 ReviewPoint Domain transaction test. Complete role/scope, remaining error/recovery, and discard-browser coverage remain open. Also open: 75 partially reviewed source/action rows awaiting full parity evidence, 28 supporting files with partial reviews, direct query/search/count/export/command retry/idempotency authorization, broader planning parity, production-like rollback/canary, screen-reader/wider-locale acceptance, live Microsoft gates and separate owner acceptance. Blazor retirement remains NOT_READY.
